Level C

Carrying Capacity: Inventory

Create a container class and integrate it with Player

What You'll Learn

1 Implement composition — Player "has-a" Inventory
2 Use a class variable as a static constraint
3 Apply encapsulation with protected attributes
4 Write accessor methods that protect internal data

Key Terms

Term Definition
Composition A "has-a" relationship where one object contains another
Encapsulation Bundling data with methods that operate on it, hiding internals
Class Variable A variable shared by all instances of a class
Accessor Method A method that provides controlled access to internal data
Protected Attribute An attribute prefixed with _ to indicate it's internal

OOP Spotlight: Encapsulation + Access Modifiers

Python does not enforce access modifiers like Java or C#, so we use conventions:

  • Public: health (no underscore)
  • Protected (convention): _items (single underscore)
  • Private-ish: __items (name mangling)

Encapsulation means: access data through methods like add() and list_items(), not by modifying _items directly.

Composition vs Aggregation: Inventory is composed inside Player (owned). Aggregation is when an object uses another object without owning its lifetime.

Class Design (UML)

◆ Composition (owns the object)
_ Protected/internal attribute

Structure Guide

Click each section to expand. Build the Inventory class first, then integrate it with Player.

1 Class Definition & Class Variable
CLASS Inventory:
MAX_CAPACITY = 10
This is a class variable — shared by all Inventory instances, not unique to each one. It defines the maximum number of items any inventory can hold.
2 Constructor
CONSTRUCTOR():
Must do:
  • Create an empty list called _items
The underscore prefix indicates this is a protected attribute — accessed through methods, not directly.
3 add
METHOD add(item_id) → boolean:
Returns: True if item was added, False otherwise

Must check:
  • Is the inventory already full?
  • Is this item already in the inventory?
Only add the item if both checks pass.
4 remove
METHOD remove(item_id) → boolean:
Returns: True if item was removed, False if not found
5 Accessor Methods
METHOD list_items() → list:
Returns a copy of _items, not the list itself. This protects encapsulation.
METHOD has_item(item_id) → boolean:
Returns True if item_id is in the inventory.
METHOD is_full() → boolean:
Returns True if count equals MAX_CAPACITY.
METHOD count() → integer:
Returns the number of items currently held.
6 Integrate with Player
Update your Player class constructor to create an Inventory:
this.inventory = NEW Inventory()

This is composition — the Player now "has-a" Inventory.
